reason: E2 directly demonstrates phase-selective recrystallization in a EHEA, achieving ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress by eliminating weak boundaries and fully releasing strain hardening, which supports the core premises. E1 provides background on lamellar fcc+B2 EHEAs and dislocation-pile-up strengthening but does not address recrystallization or ductility enhancement, so it offers only indirect context.
premises: Phase-selective recrystallization can be achieved in lamellar eutectic high-entropy alloys by tailored annealing
Recrystallizing the ductile phase smooths internal phase boundaries and reduces dislocation pile-ups
Reducing dislocation pile-ups delays microcracking and enhances room-temperature tensile ductility
The hard phase framework is retained during selective recrystallization, preserving strength
The proposed treatment yields uniform elongation ~35% and true stress ~2 GPa in a EHEA
